inlines.value: Kafka JMX environment variables in Docker
Kafka Connect JMX environment variables in Docker
You can use the JMX metrics provided by

to monitor Debezium. To use these metrics, you must enable them when you start the Kafka and Kafka Connect services. Enabling JMX involves setting the correct environment variables. The environment variables that you must set depend on whether you are running Kafka and Kafka Connect in a local installation or in Docker containers.
If you are running multiple services on the same machine, be sure to use distinct JMX ports for each service.
In addition to the built-in support for JMX metrics in Kafka and Kafka Connect, each connector provides additional metrics that you can use to monitor their activities.
With Kafka and Kafka Connect, you enable JMX by setting the appropriate environment variables when you start each service.

If you are running Kafka and Kafka Connect via the Debezium container images, enabling JMX requires several additional environment variables that are not typically needed when running on a local machine. This is because the JVM requires the host name to which it will advertise itself to JMX clients. Thus, Debezium’s container images for Kafka and Kafka Connect use several environment variables to enable and configure JMX. Most of the environment variables are the same for all of the images, but there are some minor differences.

The following example Docker command starts a container using the
environment variables, and maps the Docker host’s port 9011 to the container’s JMX port:

$ docker run -it --rm --name kafka --hostname kafka \
  -p 9092:9092 -p 9011:9011 \
  -e CLUSTER_ID=<YOUR_UNIQUE_CLUSTER_IDENTIFIER> \
  -e NODE_ID=1 \
  -e NODE_ROLE=combined \
  -e KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS=1@kafka:9093 \
  -e KAFKA_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092,CONTROLLER://kafka:9093 \
  -e KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092 \
  -e JMXPORT=9011 \
  -e JMXHOST=10.0.1.10\
  quay.io/debezium/kafka:{debezium-docker-label}
